title: Why Every Developer Needs to Learn Prompt Engineering Now
angle: Prompt engineering is not a soft skill for non-coders — it is the new bash scripting, and developers who ignore it are writing slower, dumber code right now.

scenes.voiceover: Your junior dev using ChatGPT just outpaced you. Not because they're smarter. Because they know this.
scenes.visual_description: Bold white text explodes onto black screen word by word. Final word 'THIS' flashes red three times.

scenes.voiceover: Prompt engineering is not ChatGPT tricks. It is how you turn an LLM into a compiler for your ideas.
scenes.visual_description: Split screen: left shows a vague prompt with mediocre output, right shows a structured prompt producing clean production-ready code instantly.

scenes.voiceover: Role. Context. Constraints. Output format. Four inputs. That is the entire framework. Most devs skip three of them.
scenes.visual_description: Each word of the framework slams onto screen like a terminal command being typed. Wrong-answer X marks flash for each skipped step.

scenes.voiceover: Watch. Same task. Bad prompt takes 11 back-and-forths. Structured prompt nails it in one shot. Every time.
scenes.visual_description: Time-lapse of a messy multi-message thread vs a single perfectly-answered prompt. Counter ticks up to 11 on the left. Counter shows 1 on the right, highlighted in green.

scenes.voiceover: By 2026 job listings already say prompt engineering required. This is not optional anymore. It is table stakes.
scenes.visual_description: Rapid cuts of real job listing screenshots with prompt engineering highlighted in yellow. Final cut zooms into the word REQUIRED in bold.
scenes.caption_overlay: It is already in job listings.

scenes.voiceover: Your junior is not smarter. They just learned this first. The question is — are you going to let them stay ahead?
scenes.visual_description: Text fades in slow: 'Still think it is just a ChatGPT trick?' Final frame mirrors the opening black screen with the same red flash on the word 'trick'.

hook_test.format_reference: Wait, what? — Hook with surprising claim → proof → bigger reveal
hook_test.viral_proof: The 'someone less experienced is beating you because of one skill' hook is a proven 10M+ format. Channels like Fireship and TechLead have used subordinate-surpassing-senior framing to drive 15M-40M views. The asymmetry triggers immediate ego threat response, which is the strongest scroll-stopper in tech content.
hook_test.why_it_works: Developers have strong professional identity. Threatening that identity in second one with a peer comparison forces a defensive stop-scroll. The video then resolves the threat by offering the skill gap explanation and a learnable fix, converting ego threat into actionable relief — the dopamine loop that drives saves and shares.
